# Create and manage an HCP account

Learn how to create an HCP account, manage your account settings, and remove your account.

## Overview

An HCP account gives you access to HCP services and products, including HCP Terraform, and HashiCorp community resources such as tutorials. You can create an account using your GitHub account or IBMid. After creating an account, you can manage your sign-in methods and multi-factor authentication (MFA) from your account settings.

<Warning>

Email and password sign-in is deprecated and will be removed from HCP on January 31, 2027. Before that date, add IBMid or GitHub as a sign-in method for your account. If you use SAML SSO, you must also update the SSO Sign-On URL in your identity provider. Refer to [Set up SAML SSO](/hcp/docs/hcp/iam/sso/setup/saml) for instructions.

</Warning>

### HashiCorp products and resources

You can also use your HCP credentials to sign in to the following HashiCorp products and educational resources:

- [HCP Terraform](https://cloud.hashicorp.com/products/terraform): Refer to the [HCP Terraform documentation](/terraform/cloud-docs/users-teams-organizations/users#log-in-with-your-hcp-account) to learn how to log in with your HCP credentials.
- [Tutorials](/hcp/tutorials): Step-by-step tutorials to learn HCP and other HashiCorp products
- [Discuss](https://discuss.hashicorp.com): Discussion forums where you can ask questions and product announcements
- [HashiConf virtual events](https://hashiconf.com): Resources for HashiCorp's bi-annual conference

## Requirements

Only users who created HCP accounts through GitHub or with their IBMid can [remove their accounts](#remove-your-account) in the HCP UI. SSO users, including SCIM-provisioned users, cannot remove their own accounts using the portal. If you authenticate using SSO, contact your organization administrator so that they can de-provision your account through your identity provider.

If your organization uses SSO, HashiCorp recommends maintaining at least two non-SSO users with administrative access. If all non-SSO administrative users are removed and SSO is later disabled, no local user will have sufficient permissions to administer the organization. Refer to [Single sign-on (SSO) overview](/hcp/docs/hcp/iam/sso) for more information.

Contact [IBM support](https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/node/7260345) if no administrative users are able to log in.

## Create an account

Set up single sign-on (SSO) through GitHub, IBM, or your identity provider (IdP). Visit the [login page](https://portal.cloud.hashicorp.com/sign-in) and click one of the following options:

- **Continue with IBMid**: Choose this option and follow the prompts to create an account with your IBMid. Refer to [Sign in with your IBMid](#sign-in-with-your-ibmid) for next steps.
- **Continue with GitHub**: Choose this option and follow the prompts to create an account with your GitHub account. Refer to [Sign in with your GitHub account](#sign-in-with-your-github-account) for next steps.
- **Sign-in**: Choose this option if SSO is configured through your identity provider. You can configure SSO over SAML or OIDC. Refer to the [single sign-on documentation](/hcp/docs/hcp/iam/sso) for instructions.

To automate user provisioning, de-provisioning, and other user management tasks from your IdP, refer to [SCIM provisioning](/hcp/docs/hcp/iam/scim).

## Sign in with your IBMid

You can use an IBMid to sign in to HCP. IBMid lets you use the same account you use with other IBM products and is required to open support cases with IBM.

If you do not have an IBMid, create one at [ibm.com/account/reg/signup](https://www.ibm.com/account/reg/signup).

### Add an IBMid to your existing HCP account

If you have an existing HCP account created with an email and password, you must add your IBMid as a sign-in method before January 31, 2027, and begin signing in with your IBMid to ensure access.

To check your sign-in methods, go to **Account settings** and review the **Sign-in method** setting.

The first time you sign in with your IBMid, HCP attempts to match your IBMid email to an existing HCP account email. If your existing HCP account email matches your IBMid email, HCP automatically recognizes your IBMid as a sign-in method for your existing account. Because email and password sign-in is deprecated, you should log in with your IBMid. Your organization memberships, roles, and resource access are unchanged.

If your IBMid email is different from your HCP account email, IBMid creates a new, separate HCP account. Follow the steps in [Sign in with IBMid using a different email address](#sign-in-with-ibmid-using-a-different-email-address) to grant your IBMid access to your existing organization.

### GitHub and IBMid sign-in

If your IBMid email matches your HCP account email, HCP automatically recognizes your IBMid as a sign-in method for your existing account. You can sign in with your IBMid or GitHub account. Either sign in method provides the same access.

If your IBMid email is different from your HCP account email, IBMid creates a new, separate HCP account. Follow the steps in [Sign in with IBMid using a different email address](#sign-in-with-ibmid-using-a-different-email-address) to grant your IBMid access to your existing organization.

### GitHub-only sign-in

You can create an IBMid with a GitHub account. HCP treats your IBMid and your GitHub login as two separate identities. If your HCP account uses GitHub sign-in only, signing in with IBMid always creates a new, separate HCP account. This applies even when you use your GitHub account to sign in to IBMid because that credential is for IBMid only and does not connect to your HCP GitHub authentication.

Follow the steps in [Sign in with IBMid using a different email address](#sign-in-with-ibmid-using-a-different-email-address) to grant your IBMid access to your existing organization.

### Sign in with IBMid using a different email address

If signing in with IBMid creates a separate HCP account because the email addresses do not match, complete the following steps to grant your IBMid access to your existing organization.

1. Sign in to HCP with IBMid. HCP creates a separate account for this IBMid.
1. Sign out, then sign back in using your existing sign-in method.
1. Invite your IBMid account as a new member of your HCP organization and assign the appropriate permissions. Refer to [Invite users to an organization](/hcp/docs/hcp/iam/users#invite-users).
1. Optionally, remove your old account from HCP if you prefer to sign in with a single account.

After adding IBMid to your account, you can continue to sign in with email and password until January 31, 2027. Start signing in with IBMid before that date.

## Sign in with your GitHub account

You can use a GitHub account to sign in to HCP. The steps depend on whether your GitHub account email matches your HCP account email.

### Sign in when email addresses match

At the HCP login screen, click the **GitHub** sign-in option. HCP automatically recognizes the matching email and adds GitHub as a sign-in method for your existing account. Your organization memberships, roles, and resource access are unchanged.

### Sign in with GitHub using a different email address

Signing in with GitHub creates a new, separate HCP account. Complete the following steps to grant your GitHub account access to your existing organization:

1. Sign out of HCP, then sign back in with your existing method.
1. Invite your GitHub account as a new member of your HCP organization and assign the appropriate permissions. Refer to [Invite users to an organization](/hcp/docs/hcp/iam/users#invite-users).

### Sign in without an existing GitHub account

Complete the following steps to create a GitHub account and sign in to HCP:

1. Create a GitHub account at [github.com/signup](https://github.com/signup) using the same email address as your HCP account.
1. Sign in to HCP using the **GitHub** option.

If you want a single identity for HCP, consider using an IBMid that authenticates with GitHub. IBMid gives you access to IBM support cases while letting you use GitHub to sign in.

When HashiCorp publishes an update to the HashiCorp GitHub application, GitHub may ask you to reauthorize the application, even if you previously authorized it to sign in with your GitHub account.

## Manage account settings

You can review your account settings, manage email preferences, and enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) from your account settings screen.

Choose **Account settings** from your user profile menu to review basic information about your account.

Click **Security** in the sidebar to access additional features. You can click **Enable MFA** to begin setting up MFA. Refer to the [Multi-factor authentication](/hcp/docs/hcp/iam/mfa) documentation for next steps.

## Remove your account

You can remove your HashiCorp account from HCP, end your active sessions, and delete data associated with HCP. If you use your HashiCorp account to sign in to HCP Terraform, removing your account also removes your access to HCP Terraform. To regain access, sign in again with the same credentials.

<Warning>

Account removal cannot be undone. HCP immediately removes your access to organizations, projects, and resources associated with your account.

</Warning>

### Resolve ownership dependencies

Before removing your account, HCP performs an automated check and blocks removal if you are the owner of one or more HCP organizations. You must resolve all ownership dependencies before your account can be removed.

To resolve an ownership block, complete one of the following actions for each organization you own:

- Assign the owner role to another user in the organization. Refer to [Access management](/hcp/docs/hcp/iam/access-management) for instructions.
- Complete the organization deletion checklist and delete the organization. Refer to [Delete an organization](/hcp/docs/hcp/admin/orgs#delete-an-organization) for instructions.

### Remove your account

After completing the preflight checks and resolving any ownership dependency blocks, complete the following steps to remove your account:

1. From your user profile menu, choose **Account settings**.
1. In the **Remove account** section, click **Remove my account**.
1. If your account is not eligible for removal, HCP prompts you with actions to take before you can proceed. Resolve any blocking conditions, and then repeat this procedure.
1. In the confirmation dialog, type `REMOVE` to confirm, then click **Remove my account**.

Your account is removed from HCP and you are redirected to the HCP sign-in page.
